decisions.reason: Having survived the initial launch period and fitting tightly with the firm's psychiatric core, the program likely meets aspiration levels closely enough that management keeps it.
As an outpatient extension of the core support portfolio, sociotherapy is a plausible satisfactory performer and boundedly rational management would continue it while refining demand and routines.
Its strategic fit with senior-care capabilities and earlier prominence suggest results at or above aspiration, so there is little reason to redeploy resources away from it.
The retail shop is more peripheral and easier to cut if results lag, but its sheltered-workshop and mission fit, together with organisational slack, still justify keeping it for now.
Meal delivery is close to the senior-services offer but still young and operationally uncertain, so management would usually retain it for another year unless clear underperformance emerges.
